examples.trans: Hello, Vika, where are you right now?

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'inner' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.trans: He has a powerful inner resilience.
This is the internal order of our institution.

examples.text: У меня просто мощный внутренний ресурс.
examples.trans: I simply have a powerful inner resilience.

meanings.note: pointing at something a little way off
Secondary conversational sense ('out!') (вон отсюда! = get out of here!) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'at all'.
Secondary conversational sense ('in general') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I have no idea at all.

examples.text: Я человек чистый. Я вообще не вор.
examples.trans: I'm an honest man. I'm not a thief at all.

meanings.note: ends a conversation or an order: 'Всё, свободен' = that's all, you can go
Secondary conversational sense ('that's it, done') (at the start of a sentence) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

выходить.gloss: to go out, to get out

meanings.en: to go out, to come out
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go out, to get out', paired with 'выйти'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to get out (of prison, arrest)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm going out in a minute.

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.

examples.text: Давай быстрее выходи из подсобки, начинается вечерняя смена!
examples.trans: Come on out of the storage room quickly, the evening shift is starting!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'where'.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('stupid, silly, foolish').

examples.text: Ваня, ты глупый? Зачем ты сейчас это при нём сказал?
examples.trans: Vanya, are you stupid? Why did you just say that in front of him?

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to give', forming an aspectual pair with 'давать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Derived feminine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'girl'.

examples.trans: In short, girls, listen to me.
Girl, pass me the sugar, please.

meanings.en: to guess, to work out, to think of
meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'гадаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to guess, to realise', paired with 'догадываться'.

examples.trans: Why didn't I think of it at once!

examples.text: Какой глупый человек догадался это сделать?
examples.trans: What foolish person thought of doing that?

examples.text: Ты никогда сам не догадаешься об этом.
examples.trans: You will never guess this by yourself.

meanings.note: affectionate form of дочь; also used by older people to address a young woman

examples.text: Мой Гриша мечтать об этом не мог! Спасибо, дочка!
examples.trans: My Grisha could not even dream of this! Thank you, dear!

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'recording', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('written note, appointment') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I listened to the recording of the conversation.

examples.text: Кто здесь снимает? Кто оператор? Запись идёт?
examples.trans: Who is filming here? Who is the cameraman? Is it recording?

звонить.gloss: to call, to phone; to ring

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to call', forming an aspectual pair with 'позвонить'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to ring') (a bell or phone) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
large structure such as an office, school, or hall

examples.text: На огромной скорости машина врезалась в здание!
examples.trans: At huge speed the car crashed into the building!
This is an old, beautiful building.

examples.text: Пятнадцать лет мы просим новое здание!
examples.trans: For fifteen years we've been asking for a new building!

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('what') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'camera', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Of course, everything is recorded on camera.

examples.text: Нужно ходить по городу с камерой!
examples.trans: You need to walk around town with a camera!

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).
Secondary conversational sense ('cuisine, cooking') (русская кухня = Russian cuisine) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Three rooms and a big kitchen.
And the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: мам! = casual 'Mum!' when calling her

Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'can', forming an aspectual pair with 'смочь'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to find', paired with 'находить'.

examples.text: Ну где я сейчас найду грузчиков?
examples.trans: Well, where am I going to find movers right now?

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
+ genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
Secondary conversational sense ('there isn't') (+ genitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

отключить.gloss: to switch off, to cut off

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'ключить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to switch off', forming an aspectual pair with 'отключать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to cut off (power, water)') (отключить свет = cut the power) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: И позвони Цыганкову, пусть отключат свет.
examples.trans: And phone Tsygankov, have them cut the power.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'from here'.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

перевернуть.gloss: to tip over, to turn over

meanings.en: to tip over, to overturn, to flip
meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'вернуть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to tip over, to turn over', paired with 'переворачивать'.

examples.text: На Московской улице перевернули ящики с мусором.
examples.trans: On Moskovskaya Street someone tipped over the rubbish bins.
The cat tipped over the water bowl.

examples.text: Так пойдём, давай вернёмся! Я всё переверну!
examples.trans: Then let's go, let's go back! I'll turn everything upside down!

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to go', forming an aspectual pair with 'идти'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: подписать приказ = to sign an order

examples.text: Я их ещё два года назад им выделил! Я сам приказ подписывал!
examples.trans: I allocated it to them two years ago! I signed the order myself!

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'казать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to order', forming an aspectual pair with 'приказывать'.

examples.text: А Клавдия Викторовна приказала сделать ей массаж ног!
examples.trans: And Klavdia Viktorovna ordered me to give her a foot massage!
The general ordered the gates to be opened.
He ordered our operation to continue.

meanings.en: to check, to test, to verify
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'верить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to check, to test', paired with 'проверять'.

examples.text: Вот с таким настроением и иди к Аникееву. Паяльник проверь.
examples.trans: Go to Anikeev in just that mood. Check the soldering iron.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('oneself') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to do', forming an aspectual pair with 'делать'.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Secondary conversational sense ('in a moment') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: общественный совет = public council
Secondary conversational sense ('piece of advice') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Это правильно. Я приглашаю вас в общественный совет.
examples.trans: That's right. I'm inviting you onto the public council.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'транный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('strange, odd').
'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I
Secondary conversational sense ('? = what's this?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
International compound from Greek 'tele' (far) + 'phone' (voice, sound).

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'now'.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'too'.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Secondary conversational sense ('exactly, precisely') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я точно не помню его адрес.
examples.trans: I don't remember his exact address.

examples.text: Точно, полиция была! А что с машиной?
examples.trans: That's right, the police were there! And what about the car?

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'toilet', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: The toilet is in the corridor.
Do you remember the toilet in the communal flat?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'at' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('I have') (possession) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('from (ask from someone)') (просить у кого) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: instrumental of утро used as an adverb

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'well'.
Secondary conversational sense ('good, fine') (as an answer) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Хорошо, Виктор Петрович, я сейчас же всё переделаю заново!
examples.trans: All right, Viktor Petrovich, I will redo everything right now!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'worse'.

examples.text: Ваня, всё гораздо хуже. Меня обманули.
examples.trans: Vanya, it's much worse than that. I've been cheated.

meanings.note: the plural is a different word: люди, людям, о людях
Secondary conversational sense ('people') (plural люди, a different word) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!
